# Variables

The session's Python namespace is shared by the agent (`r1`, …), the SmashDb console (`q1`, …) and the
cells. The Variables pane shows what is in it and clears it. This says what must hold;
`experimental/reflex-kernel/README.md` says what is built.

## Rules

- **Cleared means gone.** A cleared name is removed from Python at once, exactly as `del` would, and its tab
  closes. The user expects the memory back, so the app must not keep the object alive behind their back.
- **Undo is short and single.** One batch, the last clear, can be put back for a few seconds
  (`variables.UNDO_SECONDS`). After that, or on `Free now`, or on the next clear, the batch is dropped for
  good: no history of clears, nothing kept "just in case".
- **A purge drops every holder the app has**, not only the name: `_`, a cell result showing the object, a
  tool call's record of it (`Session.purge`). A new place that keeps a value by reference must be added
  there, and to the test that checks a cleared DataFrame is really freed
  (`tests/experimental/reflex_kernel/test_variables.py`, the `weakref` one).
- **Undo never overwrites.** A name bound to something new since the clear stays as it is now, and the
  user is told which names were not put back.
- **What the user still holds is theirs.** An object bound to another name (`a = r1`) is not touched by
  clearing one of its names, and isn't counted as freed.
- **Be honest about what can't be freed.** Where the app has to keep an object (an agent result that is a
  model is part of the chat history), the pane or the README says so rather than claiming it was freed.
- **`r` numbers are never reused.** The chat refers to results by name; a cleared `r2` must not come back
  as a different table.
- **One rule for "the user's variables"** (`perf.user_variables`): public names that are data. Modules,
  functions and classes only on request; `pl`, `db` and `_names` never. The pane and the debug panel's
  System tab both read it.
- **Not a cache.** The held batch is the original objects on their way out; nothing is served from it.
  Keeping cleared values longer (a history, a recycle bin) would need the user's approval first, as any
  cache does (`.agents/agents.md`, "Caching Policy").

## Mentions (`@name`, experimental)

`@q1` in a chat box points at a variable: the AI is told what it holds. Started Nov 2026 on the branch
`exp/at-variables` (`reflex_kernel/mentions.py`); ideas not built are in `personal/ai/at-variable-mentions.md`.

- **Chats only, for now**: the chat, a tool form's Ask AI row (so `/vods <text>` too) and an editor's inline
  chat. Not form fields, cells or the SQL box.
- **A variable or plain text.** `@name` is a mention only when `name` is one of the user's variables (the rule
  above, `perf.user_variables`). Anything else (`@someone`, an email) is sent as typed, with no error.
- **Nothing is called.** A dotted path (`@r3.df`, `@q1.char`) follows columns, fields, keys and attributes;
  never a method, never a private name. It is followed as far as it names something: the rest is the sentence.
- **Small goes whole, big goes as a summary** (`mentions.WHOLE_ROWS`, `WHOLE_CHARS`): a big table is its shape,
  columns and first rows, and the text says it is not all there. The AI must never be left thinking a cut
  value is the whole one.
- **Only the chat agent can read further**, with `query_variable` (SQL on the variable; its result is a new
  `r<n>`). The app adds that tool on each run: `pkgs/ds/ai` doesn't know of it. The inline AIs keep "no tools"
  (`inline_ai.md`), so there a big variable is its summary.
- **A snapshot.** The AI gets the value as it is when the message is sent. Binding the name to something new
  later doesn't change what was sent.
- **Text only: no new holder.** A mention gives the AI text and keeps no object, so "cleared means gone" holds
  with no change to `Session.purge` (tested with a `weakref`, as clearing is). The text stays in the chat
  history, as a tool result's CSV does.
- **Not a cache.** The text is built again on every send.
- **Only mentions = print, no AI.** A message that is nothing but mentions (`@q1`) shows them in the chat and
  asks no model; the agent never gets those rows (as a slash command's).
- **Through the AI into a widget.** A variable reaches another widget's inputs by the inline AI reading it and
  proposing inputs, which the user runs (`inline_ai.md`). Typing `@name` into a form field does nothing.
- **Coloured as a slash command is, in another colour** (purple; a slash command is blue), where it is typed
  in the chat box and in the chat's row of what was mentioned.

## `/assign`: a variable written by the AI

`/assign [name =] <what it should hold>` in the chat makes a new variable (`reflex_kernel/assign.py`).

- **The AI writes code, the user runs it.** The proposal is the Python that makes the variable, shown in the
  chat to read and change. Nothing runs until the user does it (Enter); Esc drops it. As everywhere, the AI
  proposes and the user runs (`inline_ai.md`).
- **Code, for what it shows, never at the cost of the answer.** Code that computes from the session's data is
  exact and says where a value comes from, so it is preferred. What can't be computed is still allowed: the
  AI writes what it knows as a literal (`release = datetime.date(2018, 12, 7)`). The proposal says which of
  the two it is, because a literal is the model's memory and is not checked.
- **Structured values only**: a basic value (`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `date`, `datetime`, `time`,
  `timedelta`), a list of basic values of one kind, a pydantic model whose fields are those, or a polars
  DataFrame. **Never a dict**, and no `None`, tuple, set, Series or list of records (several records are a
  DataFrame). The check is on the value the code made (`assign.value_problem`), so it holds for code the user
  changed too.
- **A record is a pydantic model**, not a dataclass: the app already shows one as fields, a mention sends one
  as JSON, and its field types are checked. Its class is defined by the code and stays in the session.
- **Nothing is bound unless all of it worked.** The code runs in a copy of the namespace: a failure or a
  refused value leaves the session as it was, and helper names the code made don't stay.
- **The name is the user's when given** (`/assign top5 = ...`), else the AI's, and it can be changed in the
  code before running. An existing name is replaced, as in Python, and the chat says so.
- **It reads, it doesn't look up.** The chat so far, the session's variables and `@` mentions, the SmashDb
  tables. No tools: a fact it should check belongs in a chat turn first.

## Not done yet

- **Rename** (`r3` → `mac_h2h`), with the tab, tool form and debug-log link following the name.
- **Clear by group** (only agent results, only saved queries, only your own names) and **pin** (kept by
  `Clear all`): the user chose select all / deselect all instead, for now.
- **A filter box** over the list, as Omarchy's menus have (`spec/experimental/reflex-kernel/omarchy.md`).
- **The chat agent only knows the variables you mention** (`@q1`, above). It has no list of what exists, so
  "the table I saved" without an `@` means nothing to it.
- **A `/assign` variable doesn't keep its code.** The code stays in the chat row; the Variables pane only
  says it came from `/assign`. Showing the code there (and running it again) needs a record that follows the
  value through clear, undo and a rebind.
- **Nothing survives a backend restart.** Variables live in server memory only; keeping them is a data
  storage question (`spec/pkgs/ds/data/data_storage.md`), not this pane's.
